title: Information for Proportional Effects in Capacity-Limited Micro-Randomized Trials

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the exact information and capacity-duration frontier for an exogenous known-variance Gaussian MRT model, with finite score-reversal and treatment-driven eligibility witnesses. The protocol-level Bellman result is conditional on a shared reward decomposition, so the field-level bridge to an intended clinical protocol remains open; D0.5 delivered incremental novelty below the required field floor. The final D0 graph and rendered note were synchronized, the three panel scope and positioning findings were repaired, and only the acknowledged protocol-frontier open question remains.
tldr: A weekly treatment quota fixes assignment covariance, but neither that covariance nor the protocol kernels \(Q_t\) and \(\Omega\) identify information about the proportional causal effect. Conditional on an exogenous eligible path, the declared product-Gaussian experiment yields an exact intercept-projected score, an attaining normal estimator, a separable integer design, and the exogenous product-Gaussian replacement number \(b^{\star}\). The protocol-kernel nonidentification proposition gives an asymmetric finite pair with identical \(Q_t\) and \(\Omega\) but actual replacement indices \(\infty\) and \(1\); it does not characterize all protocols. Under separate, explicit full-likelihood conditions---policy-indexed adapted martingale score increments and finite conditional second-moment rewards common to all admissible policies---projected information is additive and a finite Bellman recursion gives an exact slot-versus-week certificate, reducing to \(b^{\star}\) on the exogenous Gaussian path. These conditions are sufficient, not maximal or necessary. A bounded known-variance likelihood reverses the reciprocal-variance quota ranking by \(2/63\), and treatment-induced eligibility defeats the myopic quota exactly when \(a_2/a_1>3/2\). No universal causal-excursion efficiency or generic water-filling novelty is claimed.
gap: Capacity-limited MRT planning currently combines simulation evidence, fixed-count designs on other dependence axes, and classical resource-allocation tools without an exact bridge from a declared across-patient weekly quota likelihood to a finite capacity--duration decision.
fill: The project supplies the Gaussian score and estimator, the integer replacement number \(b^{\star}\), the bounded score reversal, and the \(3/2\) eligibility-feedback threshold, while leaving protocol-level residual dependence as an explicit open-ended question.
